To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the biomass of various microorganisms and plants can be used as an effective biosorbent for the removal of heavy metals and the biosorbents can be reused for several times without losing their sorption capacity.
the biomass of various microbial and plant origin can be used for the removal of heavy metals and metal ions from aqueous solution.
microbial and plant derived biomasses are promising adsorbents for heavy metal removal from aqueous solution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel biosorption process for the recovery of heavy metals from industrial wastewater.
the development of an economical and eco-friendly technology for heavy metal removal from industrial effluents.
the development of a low cost biosorbent from microbial and plant biomass for the removal of heavy metal from aqueous solution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
biosorption of heavy metals from wastewaters by biomass is an attractive alternative to conventional treatment technologies.
biosorption is a potential alternative technology for treatment of metal contaminated effluents.
the biosorption of heavy metals is a promising technology and is likely to be used on a large scale for removal of heavy metal ions from aqueous solution in near future.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
biosorption process is a simple and economical technology for removal of heavy metal pollutants from wastewater.
the biomass of microorganisms and plants have great potential for heavy metal remediations and the technology can be adopted for the treatment of metal contaminated wastewater.
the biosorption technology offers an alternative and economical way of treating wastewater containing heavy metals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
microbial and plant derived biosorbent can be used as an alternative technology for the removal of heavy metals and can be used for the recovery of these metals from aqueous solutions.
biosorption of heavy metals is a promising and economically feasible method of removing toxic heavy metals from wastewater.

microbial and plant derived non living biomass can serve as a cost effective and eco-friendly alternative for heavy metal removal from aqueous solutions and may be a promising technology for the treatment of industrial effluents.
